person_made_it: It opens by telling twelve students the actual shape of their day in one sentence, then gives them the exact minute a character gets described on screen; no template knows that Critical Role's cold open ends at 18:51 or that the ad break is the trap.
emcee_who_is_speaking: One amber accent, used only for what is live: the section labels, the term numbers, the timestamps. On any screen the three terms are the only thing that can speak first.
what_time_of_day_is_this_room: A phone at 9am on the walk to SCI L104, which is why it is dark, short, and five screens instead of the professor's eight printed pages.
did_the_click_pay_me: Yes: three timestamped links that drop you at the exact second, not at the top of a four and a half hour video.
works_for_the_recipient: 805 words, 5.1 phone screens, no JavaScript, no calendar, no names, nothing on it that would embarrass anyone if a student forwarded it.
taught_me_something: That telling students the exit ticket questions in advance is free and makes the answers better, and that naming the three things they already carry beats saying no homework, which a room hears as free evening.
told_me_the_truth: Yes, including that the timestamps come from caption tracks and point at speech, so scrub a few seconds either side if the moment has moved.
weakest: It asserts that the mood board is where the vocabulary gets used without showing a single example of a sentence doing it well; one real before-and-after line would teach more than the paragraph explaining the idea.
